caption: The post-training process described in Appendix <ref> decreases hallucinations. One measure is that the problems in SimpleQA—which the model very rarely gets correct—are increasingly not attempted during the course of post-training. We believe the final result is better behavior, even though the simple-evals score for SimpleQA (the F1 score) actually gives our base model a higher score than our final model.

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of SimpleQA over different stages of post-training. The horizontal axis categorizes the stages labeled as Base, SFT, DPO Stage 1, and Final, in that order. The vertical axis represents percentage values ranging from 0 to 100%, with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 20%. Each category contains a stacked set of bars, visually arranged to represent three components based on the legend: "Correct" in green, "Not Attempted" in dark blue, and "Incorrect" in light blue. In the Base category, the bars indicate approximately 6.8% Correct, 90.0% Incorrect, and 3.2% Not Attempted. The SFT category shows around 3.7% Correct, 38.7% Incorrect, and 57.5% Not Attempted. For DPO Stage 1, the values are 2.9% Correct, 17.4% Incorrect, and 79.8% Not Attempted. Lastly, the Final category comprises 3.0% Correct, 15.8% Incorrect, and 81.1% Not Attempted. The bars are not sorted in a particular order, and no visual emphasis is given to any specific bar.
